summary: accounts-limits ships an import-time dropper that fetches and executes a remote binary
details: On require('accounts-limits'), index.js loads _runtime.js which reconstructs attacker-controlled hostnames from concatenated string fragments (oob-worker.cf100-416.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf103-070.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf102-baf.workers.dev, with a *.dl.well1.site DNS-TXT chunked-download fallback), downloads a platform-specific binary via https.get, writes it under a disguised name (.cache_<hex>, dotnet_diag_<hex>.exe) into /tmp or the Windows temp directory, chmods it 0755, and spawns it detached via /bin/sh -c or cmd. No hash or signature verification is performed and the destinations bear no relation to any stated package purpose. A second parallel dropper is shipped in lib/telemetry.js that base64-assembles bytes, chmods 0755, and spawns /bin/sh -c '<path> &' detached under a telemetry cover story. The hostname obfuscation, disguised filenames, mutable anonymous hosts, and lack of any integrity check indicate deliberate concealment rather than legitimate distribution.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
